# Green Party Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Overview
The Green Party's 2024 manifesto addresses the cost-of-living crisis, climate emergency, and deteriorating public services. Co-leaders Carla Denyer and Adrian Ramsay present policies they argue will create a fairer, greener country through ambitious investment and systemic reform.

## Health and Social Care
The party proposes £28bn additional annual NHS funding by 2030, plus £20bn capital investment over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing GP access, ensuring universal NHS dentistry (£3bn annually by 2030), boosting staff pay, and restoring public health budgets. They pledge to reverse NHS privatisation through the NHS Reinstatement Bill and introduce free personal social care with £20bn annual investment.

## Housing
The manifesto promises 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering councils to introduce rent controls, and ending no-fault evictions. A major retrofit programme (£29bn over five years) would insulate homes to high standards, reducing energy bills and emissions.

## Energy and Climate
Green MPs would push for wind to provide 70% of electricity by 2030, end new oil and gas licences, introduce a carbon tax starting at £120/tonne, and bring energy companies into public ownership. They reject nuclear power as expensive and slow compared to renewables.

## Economy and Work
The party proposes £40bn average annual green investment, bringing utilities into public ownership, taxing wealth fairly (including a wealth tax on assets over £10m), and reforming capital gains tax. Workers' rights would be strengthened with a £15 minimum wage, maximum 10:1 pay ratios, and restored union rights.

## Welfare and Education
Universal Credit would increase by £40/week, the two-child cap abolished, and disability benefits increased 5%. Education reforms include scrapping tuition fees, restoring maintenance grants, £8bn school investment, and abolishing Ofsted.

## Transport
Public transport subsidies would reach £10bn annually, railways would return to public ownership, and £2.5bn yearly would fund cycling and walking infrastructure. Aviation would face a frequent-flyer levy.

## Environment and Nature
A Rights of Nature Act would give nature legal personhood. The party commits to 30% of land and seas protected by 2030, water companies nationalised, and harmful pesticides banned.

## Democracy and International Affairs
Reforms include proportional representation, votes at 16, and replacing the House of Lords. Internationally, the party supports rejoining the EU, signing the UN nuclear weapons ban, and increasing overseas aid to 1% of GNI. On Israel-Palestine, they demand an immediate ceasefire and recognition of Palestine.

## Funding
Revenue would come from wealth taxes (£50-70bn annually by parliament's end), carbon taxes (up to £80bn), and business tax reforms. The party accepts deficit spending for green investment, rejecting conventional fiscal rules while monitoring inflation.
